item.title: China sets a lower economic growth target of 4.5% to 5% for 2026 as challenges loom
item.description: China has set an economic growth target of 4.5% to 5% for this year, a slight decrease in the face of a prolonged property slump and other headwinds and global uncertainty. The target was announced Thursday in an annual report presented by Premier Li Qiang at the opening session of this year’s meeting of the National People’s Congress. item.title: Honduras weighs shift in China-Taiwan ties as Trump pushes for US dominance in Latin America
item.description: The new president of Honduras, who was elected with the backing of President Donald Trump, has ordered a review of economic agreements with China. This has fueled expectations that Honduras will distance itself from Beijing, in line with a Trump administration campaign to reduce Chinese economic clout in Latin America. item.title: War with Iran chokes flows of oil and natural gas, highlighting energy security risks for Asia
item.description: The war with Iran is disrupting oil and LNG shipments through the Strait of Hormuz, a key artery for global energy trade, sending prices higher and threatening global growth. The risks are highest for countries in Asia. Japan, South Korea and Taiwan depend heavily on the Middle East for their fuel, while India and China face inflation and supply risks if the conflict drags on.
